title: What CI/CD is
summary: Automated checks run on every push, and automated deployment ships code that passes. It is why teams care so much about small commits and a clean main branch.

sections.heading: CI: continuous integration
sections.body:
When you push commits to the hosting site, a robot wakes up. It downloads your branch, installs the project, runs the tests, checks formatting and sometimes security scans. This is **continuous integration (CI)**. Results show up on the pull request as green ticks or red crosses.

A red check usually blocks merging. So before a reviewer even looks, the machine has already told you whether you broke something.

sections.heading: CD: continuous delivery or deployment
sections.body:
Once a change is merged into main, another robot can build the product and put it in front of users automatically. That is **continuous deployment**. Some teams stop one step earlier and keep a button for a human to press; that is continuous delivery. Either way, main going green means the change is on its way to customers.

This is why main is protected and why a bad commit on main is treated as an incident.

sections.heading: What it means for how you use Git
sections.body:
- Small commits are easier to test and easier to undo when a check fails.
- Clear messages let the person on call understand what shipped.
- Never commit half-finished code to a shared branch; CI would run it and go red for everyone.
- Secrets must not be in the repository, because CI logs and deploys are visible to many people.

Several labs simulate a CI check so you can see these rules in action.

takeaways: CI runs automatic checks on every push and reports on the pull request.
CD ships merged code to users, often automatically.
Small, clean, well-described commits exist because of this pipeline.

quiz.question: What happens when you push a branch to a team with CI?
options: Nothing until a human runs the tests
Automated checks run and report green or red on the pull request
The code is sent to customers immediately
quiz.explanation: CI runs tests and checks automatically; deployment usually happens only after merge.

quiz.question: Why do teams insist on small commits?
options: Because Git has a size limit
Because they are easier to test, review and undo when a check fails
quiz.explanation: Small changes isolate failures and make rollbacks precise.

quiz.question: A commit with half-finished code on a shared branch would...
options: Make CI fail for everyone on that branch
quiz.explanation: CI tests whatever is pushed. Broken work on a shared branch blocks teammates.
